quote_text:
Barry, how's the heart rate? Um, it was a bit all over the place,  
I’ve been honest with you during the game, but  really proud of the effort and the commitment  
that my players showed tonight. Obviously  difficult when you get down to 10 men,  
you have to go and play two banks of four  really deep, but I thought the game plan  
that I gave them, they worked ever so hard to  make sure that it never got broken down. They  
had a couple of chances, like every very  good team is going to have against you,  
but I thought we defended really  well and we coped with their threat.
Can you make sense that a team that had  gone, I think, 10 games without keeping  
a clean sheet and losing a player so early  on tonight against one of the top teams in  
La Liga is able to keep them out, even with  nine men in what was a lengthy stoppage time? 
Well listen, it has been a problem, conceding  goals even before I came in. Since I’ve come in,  
that’s one of the areas where we’ve tried to  work really hard, and we worked really hard  
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday on it. That’s  what I want to see from my defenders  
– I want them to defend. And it’s not just about  the defenders. I need my midfield to chip in,  
and I need my forward players to chip  in. Because you’ve got to remember,  
it’s not about individuals, it’s a team sport.  And what I’ve seen tonight out there was a team  
that took the instructions on –  obviously the chat we had on Monday  
really sunk in – and they took the information  in as well, and that’s important. I think anybody  
watching the game tonight would have seen a team  that ran through brick walls for each other.
Are there any complaints for the sending off? No, I’ve seen… I can see the reason why the  
referee gave the red card. I’ve seen them given,  and I’ve seen them not given. It is what it is.  
The referee makes a decision, we just have to go  on with it. It kind of curtails our game plan,  
then we need to go back to something  different. But again, I’m proud of the guys,  
how they took that information on. It’s not ideal,  it’s not the way that we wanted to play this game,  
but I thought overall the boys, after letting them  know a few home truths on Saturday and Monday,  
I’ve got to give them a lot of credit for tonight.
Just on that Barry, you said after the  weekend’s game that you were going to  
make changes. I just wonder how tough a call  it was for you to replace Jack with Liam – and  
what a way he’s taken that opportunity. One of the toughest things I’ve had to do.  
Firstly, I think Jack Butland is a top  goalkeeper. Secondly, I’ve got a very,  
very good relationship with Jack – I’ve known  Jack a long time. He was a young kid coming  
through at Birmingham when I went down to play  for Birmingham in the Premier League. And thirdly,  
I’ve got to know it’s hurting Jack, and I’ve  got to be mindful of that as well, because I  
care for him. So I just had to make a decision,  and it was a tough decision. When I spoke to him,  
I could see he was hurting. So yeah, you go  with decisions. It’s not one that I decided  
on Saturday night or Sunday – I thought long  and hard about it. And when I spoke with him,  
it was a tough 10, 15-minute conversation.  But listen, Jack’s still got a huge part to  
play here. But in terms of Liam coming  in, I thought he did well tonight.
Liam’s obviously one of six changes  tonight from the team that started on  
Saturday. You said in the press conference  earlier this week that you would shoulder  
the responsibility for that – are you  satisfied with how the changes worked? 
Well, for 10 minutes I was satisfied,  because I had 11 men on the pitch. Then  
it kind of goes to pot. But in terms of the  changes – it’s an opportunity. I’m going to  
give people opportunities. When I’m not happy  with performances, I’m going to make changes.  
That’s just part and parcel of being a manager.  Some of them are tough at times. And again,  
a lot of people have seen an 18-year-old  kid who I think is behind in development,  
but I’ve been working really hard with Bailey for  five and a half weeks since I’ve been through the  
door. I think there’s a real footballer there  – he’s just got stuff he needs to learn. But  
I thought he handled the occasion brilliantly.  Liam coming in. The other ones – Robin obviously,  
10 minutes you lose. Leon Balogun – I know what  I’m getting from him. Ridvan’s been carrying an  
injury, come on, he’s had to come off with another  injury. But listen, I was happy with everybody,  
but also the guys that came on as well, because  they’re disappointed on the bench – but I want  
to see players disappointed because that means  they care. If I don’t play people and they’re  
laughing and joking, that’s when I’ve got a  problem. But in terms of the changes – yep,  
they came in, they’ve done their job. But also the  guys that came on did the job also for the team.
I don’t even know how many players I’ve got  available. I need to wait until tomorrow. We’re  
in tomorrow. There’s a number of guys struggling  – they’re going for scans tomorrow. There was a  
couple of guys that I risked tonight, but  I just thought it was a big occasion for  
the club and I had to go with their risks, and  they might backfire on me. I just need to wait  
and see the kind of results and the reports I  get back from the doctor and the medical staff.
We’re still in the tie. I said to them before the  game, we need to make sure we’re in this tie. And  
certainly, the tie is there for us to go and try  and get through into the semi-finals. But it’s the  
same for them – they’re still in the tie, they’re  at home. But we’ll go and give it our best shot.  
We’ll set up in a way that will try and  get us hopefully into the semi-final.
You mentioned the goalkeeper and the defence  there. I think in the second half, Bilbao had over  
80% possession but their only shot on target was  the saved penalty – how pleased are you with that? 
I couldn’t care less if they had 100% possession.  I said that to the boys – make sure we don’t  
concede, and we’ve done that. We had to play,  as I said, really low, two banks of four,  
really tight together. And if somebody jumps out  of that, then it causes us problems. But again,  
I’m delighted that they took the information  on. And it was key that we had to do that.  
But look – they’re a quality team,  you’ve seen that. They’ve got very,  
very good football players. And look, it  will be a tough one for us next Thursday.
You talked about getting the response  you wanted from your players for the  
talks earlier on in the week – but is this  just the start really? It needs to just keep  
on continuing, you need to keep on getting  the response game on game from the players. 
Yeah, I’m happy we won one game. Listen,  I’m delighted for them and I’m proud of  
them. Standing on the touchline was a totally  different feeling I had from Saturday. I felt  
empty on Saturday – the last 10, 15 minutes – just  like the stadium. But standing there at the side,  
I was proud of them. And that’s the way I  need to feel. And that’s the performances  
and the effort that this group of players need  to put in. And I’ve told them, if you do that,  
you’ve better chances of winning games of  football. And as I said, that’s what I asked,  
and that’s what I got tonight. And  that’s what I need to see going forward.
title: Why I BINNED Butland | Barry Ferguson Post Match Interview | Rangers 0-0 Athletic Bilbao
